chunks: From him, from ʿAlī ibn al-Sindī, from Ḥammād, from Shuʿayb, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: May a man perform ghusl in an open place? He said, “If no one sees him, then there is no harm.”

key_terms.إِذَا: if; introducing the condition for permissibility
key_terms.الرَّجُلُ: the man; the subject of the legal ruling
key_terms.بَارِزًا: openly or in an exposed place
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; indicating permissibility
key_terms.لَمْ يَرَهُ: no one sees him; the condition of privacy
key_terms.يَغْتَسِلُ: performs ghusl, meaning washes the body in a full ritual bath

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to perform ghusl in an open place if no one sees him?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about performing ghusl in an open or exposed place. It indicates that doing so is not objectionable so long as no one sees the person, reflecting concern for modesty and privacy.
